summary:
We developed AstraJunior, an interactive game built on Scratch to train and inspire the next generation of junior astronauts.
Our project addresses the challenge by turning complex space exploration concepts into fun, hands-on missions. Through astronaut training simulation, players learn real facts about space travel, gravity, and astronaut routines using accessible, gamified activities based on NASA resources.
This project is important because it makes space science approachable and exciting for young learners. By using a free, browser-based platform with simple visual language, we lower barriers to STEM education and empower children from any background to see themselves as future space explorers.
details:
Our game is based on space exploration, the exploration of planets, and the construction of bases on planets/moons.

It offers a brief insight into outer space and the construction of bases off planet Earth.

Teaching children and young people the simplest possible way to build a space base.

We use "Scratch" as our primary software; for programming and debugging, we use Claude Code; and the language employed is "Scratch" (the same name as the software).

We use pixel art.

We take into account the age group, target audience, and the didactic approach to gameplay.
